BIM Coordinator vs BIM Manager

Coordinators run the model process day to day; managers own the information strategy. Hiring the wrong one leaves a gap either way.

BIM coordinator and BIM manager are often used interchangeably in job adverts. They are different roles, and projects that hire one when they need the other end up with either strategy and no process, or process and no strategy.

The BIM manager

The BIM manager owns how information is produced and managed across the project or the organisation. Typical responsibilities:

  • Writing and maintaining the BIM Execution Plan with the appointed parties
  • Setting up the CDE, naming conventions, status codes and approval workflows
  • Defining LOD and information requirements by stage
  • Auditing compliance and reporting model progress and quality to project leadership
  • Managing the BIM team and its training

The BIM coordinator

The coordinator runs the model process day to day:

  • Federating discipline models and running clash tests
  • Grouping clashes, assigning them and tracking them to closure
  • Running coordination meetings and recording decisions
  • Checking models against the BEP before they are shared
  • Supporting modelers with standards and technical questions

Skills and tools

Coordinators need deep Navisworks or ACC coordination skills and a strong grasp of how trades fit together. Managers need standards knowledge (ISO 19650 workflows, BEPs, information requirements), communication with project leadership and the authority to enforce standards.

Which one does your project need?

Early stages and multi-party projects need a BIM manager to set the rules. Design development and construction need coordinators to run the process every week. Large projects need both; small ones can sometimes combine the roles in one experienced person, as long as somebody has time for the weekly coordination cycle.
